# `canopymaxima`: find tree tops {#sec-canopymaxima}

## What it does

`canopymaxima` finds individual tree tops as local height peaks on a
canopy height model, and reports each one's location and height. Tree
tops are the basis of individual-tree inventories: counting stems,
building tree lists, and matching lidar trees to field-measured trees.

A cell counts as a tree top when it is the highest cell within a search
window around it. The window grows with height, since taller trees have
wider crowns: at height *H*, its radius is `/window-a` + `/window-b` x *H*,
in the canopy model's units, rounded to whole cells and never less than
one cell.
A small window finds more tops (and splits large crowns); a large window
finds fewer (and merges small neighbouring trees).

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| (input) | `out/chm.tif` | The canopy height model from @sec-canopymodel. |
| `/output` | `out/tree_tops.csv` | The tree-top table. |
| `/minht` | `2` | Ignore peaks lower than 2 ft. |

: Options used in the `canopymaxima` example. {#tbl-options-canopymaxima}

The window coefficients were left at their defaults (`/window-a:0.5`,
`/window-b:0.05`). Tune them to the forest type and the canopy model's
cell size; a smoothed canopy model (`canopymodel /smooth`) also reduces
false tops on bumpy crowns.

## Outputs

A CSV table with one row per tree top: `TreeID`, `X`, `Y` (in the input's
coordinate system), `Height`, and `CrownDiameter` (twice the search
window radius used at that height, a rough guide to crown size rather
than a measured crown).

## Results

In @fig-canopymaxima-tops, each tree top (aqua) sits on a bright local
peak of the canopy model, with roughly one top per visible crown and no
tops in gaps below 2 ft. Several tops clustered on one crown would suggest
the window is too small; a large crown with no top would suggest it is
too large. Tops along the tile's outer edge are likely edge effects,
since an edge cell has no neighbours on one side.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/canopymaxima_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-canopymaxima confirms that at least one top was found, that
every top lies inside the tile and is at least 2 ft tall but no taller
than the tallest point, that coordinates are written in full rather than
rounded, and that each top's height equals the canopy model's value at
its location.
